findings.where: Running text across the page: the hero lede on turquoise, the Surf, Vibe and What to look for paragraphs, and the coming-soon notice on ink (desktop and phone). It is worst in the phone notice, where the first line reads "MantaHostels   is   launching   across"
findings.fault: Every paragraph is set justified. In a narrow column with no hyphenation, this pushes the words apart unevenly: some lines have wide gaps (on phone, "workers   and   long-stay   travellers", "Lively  and  social"), and the next line is set tight. The page's texture is uneven and reads like an unfinished document, not a designed guide. Brand type runs left-aligned and ragged-right everywhere else, including the nav, the headings and the Good for list.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker reading on a phone, who has to skip across uneven gaps to follow each line. The brand owner would object too, since the brand puts 'effortless' first and names 'sterile/corporate' as the enemy.

findings.where: Good for list, at the end of each wrapped line: "Yoga ·" and "Scooter riders ·" on desktop, "Long stays ·", "Budget ·" and "Scooter riders ·" on phone
findings.fault: The middot separators are part of the item before them, so a dot is left hanging at the end of a line with nothing after it. The list looks clipped, as if an item had dropped out.
findings.who_objects: A designer or brand reviewer would see it as a setting slip. A reader scanning the list may briefly look for a missing item.

findings.where: Hero banner, the region label "BALI" above the h1 (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The label is set in small spaced capitals. The project reserves uppercase for badges and filter labels, used sparingly. This is a plain eyebrow label, so it is the only uppercase text on the page and is set apart from the brand's sentence-case voice for no reason.
findings.who_objects: The brand owner, whose rules file keeps sentence case everywhere except badges and filter labels
